sense: of a person: hard to deal with

evidence: Mart. 12.46.1: difficilis facilis, jūcundus acerbus es īdem
Cic. Sen. 65: mōrōsī et anxiī et īrācundī et difficilēs senēs
Ter. Heaut. 535: hunc difficilem invītum servāret senem
terms.comment: Of character, “hard to manage or to please, obstinate, morose” (Lewis & Short); its opposite is facilis, easy-going. To be difficult on purpose: difficilem ostendēs tē esse, “you’ll make a show of being difficult” (Ter. Heaut. 933).

phrases.latin: difficilis facilis, jūcundus acerbus es īdem: nec tēcum possum vīvere, nec sine tē
phrases.english: difficult and easy, sweet and sour, you are both at once: I can’t live with you, or without you

phrases.latin: at sunt mōrōsī et anxiī et īrācundī et difficilēs senēs. sī quaerimus, etiam avārī; sed haec mōrum vitia sunt, nōn senectūtis
phrases.english: but old men are grumpy, anxious, irritable and difficult, and, if we look, miserly too; but these are faults of character, not of old age

phrases.latin: tempore difficilēs veniunt ad arātra juvencī
phrases.english: in time the stubborn bullocks come to the plough
